character_book.description: Alphas are at the top, betas are NPCs, and Omegas are naturally discriminated against.

entries.content: Betas are subordinate to Alphas and may or may not be able to impregnate Omegas. Betas are often presented as having "normal" human anatomy with none of the special attributes of Alphas or Omegas. They don't have any heat cycle and can stay in control during all sexual activities unlike alphas and betas. And they take up 70% of the population.
Alphas are generally dominant and able to impregnate Omegas. They are the most superior ones. Alphas can have more than one partner and there are 20% alphas in the whole population.

Omegas are generally lowest on the hierarchy. Male Omegas are self-lubricating and have the ability to become pregnant. Paired Alphas may be jealous and possessive of their mate while Omega may become submissive. Omegas and Alphas may go into heat and need to have sex; this may be the only time Omegas are fertile. The heat lasts for 1 to 7 days for the omega. Omegas take up 10% of the population.

The sweat glands of the omega produce a large release of pheromones to communicate the biological shift to others. The smell is particularly strong once a month, usually during the 7 days. 

The smell change indicates the high probability for a pregnancy, which usually is pretty low. The alpha has a more aggressive response to the reproduction of the omega pheromones. The omega experiences heightened arousal and increased fertility during their heat.

The mating bite is put during sex in a heat cycle, when a alpha bites the omega in their neck. If they are marked the alpha won't change but the omega can't have any more partners. If the omega has sex with someone other then the one who marked them, they will suffers from dizziness, headache, passing out, and other symptoms. This doesn't have a solution.

They work with alphas hormones that suppress the omegas' heat. There efficiency varies from person to person, they can cause allergies and sometimes side effects. There are two types of heat inhibitors: Injection and Pills. 

Injection: When the heat symptoms appear, inject it on the arm or leg. It can have some serious side effects such as dizziness, vomiting. It's necessary to not attend school or work.

Pills: Once a day, it's necessary to take them daily. It is said that these don't have any side effects.

A bulge of muscles at the base of a cock that swells either when erect or before orgasm, often to keep both individuals from separating during and after ejaculation to ensure conception. A knot, regardless of primary sex, will last anywhere between 30 minutes to an hour.

A period of 3-5 days where an Alpha will act more possessive and territorial than normal, but not specifically in need of mating with someone. Normally, rutting periods are more common after being mated, as part of a biological cycle to protect said mate.

Alphas, Omegas, and Betas all give off a very specific sort of scent as a personal marker to their primary and secondary sex. They all have the ability to scent others, which is simply the process of spreading their specific scent on another person or object (often by physically rubbing against them).
Slick is increased self-lubrication from an Omega's hole, specifically during their heat.

A structure that Omega-identified individuals build, most commonly during heat and while pregnant. It can vary in appearance, but serves a calming purpose and dates back when a nest was required to keep an omega-identified individual safe during heat and pregnancy, as it was often built specifically to be hidden. Some still consider nest-building to be part of an omega-identified individual’s courtship or heat cycle process.
A spray that can mask the pheromones of an individual's secondary gender, either by giving them no scent or covering it up with a different fragrance.

Alpha and Omega lovers may form pair bonds (often involving mating bites) with a special connection with telepathic or empathetic qualities. In some works paired Alphas may be jealous and possessive of their mate, while the Omega may become highly tied and needy.
Pheromones are the natural fragrance that is meant to entice a potential partner. For alphas, their fragrance is masculine. For omegas, their fragrance is feminine. Betas barely exude any pheromones.

The sweat glands of an omega is the most vulnerable part of their body. It is behind the nape of their neck, exuding a delicate fragrance that attracts alphas their way. This area is where a mating bite can form, for both alphas and omegas.
